entry.title: Voice-Controlled Robots and the Promise of Natural Interaction

link.title: Voice-Controlled Robots and the Promise of Natural Interaction

entry.content:
One of the most interesting developments in robotics is the idea of commanding a robot with natural language. It feels much closer to how humans interact with tools and collaborators than traditional programming interfaces. When a robot can understand instructions spoken in plain language, the barrier to use becomes much lower.

My interest in this area comes from the belief that robotics will become more accessible when systems can communicate with us in a more human way. That is why I enjoy working on projects that combine navigation, perception, and language models.
entry.summary: A short note on language-driven robot control.

entry.title: Embodied AI and the Future of Robotic Systems

link.title: Embodied AI and the Future of Robotic Systems

entry.content:
Embodied AI feels like one of the most exciting directions in robotics right now. The idea is simple but powerful: intelligence is not only something a system thinks about, but something it can act on in the world. That is what makes robots so interesting to me.

When a robot can perceive, reason, and act in a physical environment, the gap between simulation and reality becomes much smaller. That is why I am interested in combining perception, control, and language interfaces in a single system.
entry.summary: Thoughts on embodied intelligence and the role of real-world interaction.

entry.title: Why Perception Matters in Robotics
entry.content:
A robot can have a great controller and still fail if it does not understand its environment. That is why perception is so important. Whether it is a camera, an IMU, a LiDAR sensor, or a depth stream, the quality of the sensed information shapes everything else the robot does.

In my own work, I have found that perception is often the difference between an elegant experiment and a dependable system. Good sensing makes planning more grounded, control more reliable, and interaction more intuitive.
entry.summary: A short reflection on how robots depend on good sensing.

entry.title: Learning to Control Drones with a Little Help from Learning

link.title: Learning to Control Drones with a Little Help from Learning

entry.content:
I have always been drawn to systems that have to balance precision and motion. Drones are a perfect example: they are fast, unstable, and full of opportunities for good control design. My early work in this area made me appreciate how much of robotics is really about making complicated dynamics feel simple.

What excites me most is the idea that a controller is not just a mathematical trick. It is a way of giving a machine a sense of timing, stability, and awareness. That is why I keep returning to topics like MPC, trajectory optimization, and state estimation.
entry.summary: Notes from my early interest in control and aerial robotics.
